history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 409 ("Shakti Mandir", Dhanbad) — same real temple. CONFLICTING accounts of origin: jharkhand.me and a hotel travel blog say the temple was built by local residents, construction beginning in 1974 and doors opening in 1982; velpu.com claims it was built in the 15th century A.D.; a visitor review claims construction on 19 February 1997. No authoritative founding record found. The temple houses an akhand jyoti (eternal flame) said to have been brought from Vaishno Devi (some reviews say Jwala Devi, Himachal Pradesh — CONFLICT). White-marble structure with a three-tiered tower and golden spire; the main sanctum holds the Durga idol, with images of Shiva (noted as unusual given the preponderance of linga worship in Jharkhand), Krishna and other deities also present.

name: Shakti Mandir, Dhanbad
town_description: Dhanbad is the second-largest city in Jharkhand and is widely known as the Coal Capital of India, home to extensive coal mines and the headquarters of Bharat Coking Coal Limited. It is a major railway junction on the Grand Chord line and hosts the Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines), established in 1926. The city mixes an industrial character with green belts and serves as a gateway to nearby attractions like the Maithon and Panchet dams, Topchanchi Lake and the Parasnath Hills.
